stance: Amazon's provision of dedicated IP lists and distinct user-agent strings makes crawler verification a matter of verifiable network identity rather than passive directive matching.
adoption_shape: Amazon moved unilaterally to separate automated indexing from real-time user fetching across three specific identities, placing the onus on webmasters to validate incoming traffic using explicit IP endpoints rather than treating all Amazon traffic as a single entity.
new_entrants: Amazon introduced Amzn-User alongside Amazonbot and Amzn-SearchBot to distinguish and control live, user-directed fetching separately from its general automated web crawling.
watch_for: The integration of Amazon's newly published verification endpoints into standard webmaster filtering setups to differentiate live user requests from automated crawl traffic.
